discoveries: For legacy/v0 transactions, priority fees are charged from requested compute-unit limit times CU price, not actual consumed compute; overspecified CU limits cost money.

Current official docs say V1 is active on mainnet/devnet/testnet: ComputeBudget instructions are no-ops for configuration, compute and loaded-data limits must be set in the message, and priority fee is a total-lamport config value.
Duplicate instructions of the same compute-budget variant cause transaction failure for legacy/v0 processing; execution budget also has a 1.4M CU cap.
patterns: distinguish requested CU limit from consumed units
derive fee estimate from exact message/runtime version and reconcile to finalized meta.fee
sources.overlap: Veritas decodes legacy/v0 compute-budget instructions and calculates priority fee from CU price and limit. Its output type is legacy|0. Current docs establish active V1 message-level configuration. The decoder now detects V1's 0x81 prefix and returns VERITAS_UNSUPPORTED_TRANSACTION_VERSION: V1 before legacy/v0 deserialization, making the existing safe rejection explicit rather than claiming V1 support. Canonical ingestion separately retains transaction meta.fee.
risks: V1 transaction decoding and fee-component verification remain unsupported
fee projections must not infer V1 priority fees from legacy/v0 instructions
canonical actual transaction fee remains authoritative over estimates
validation: add V1 wire fixtures against an official SDK/runtime version before implementing a V1 decoder
keep explicit fail-closed behavior for unsupported V1 messages
compare estimated fees with confirmed meta.fee including failed transactions

provenance: Local Truth-X and execution economics source review
discoveries: The documented network fee is base signature fee plus prioritization fee, and is charged whether a transaction succeeds or fails.
Base fee counts transaction signatures and supported precompile signatures; priority fee formula rounds micro-lamports up, while v1 stores an absolute total priority fee in the message.
Jito tips and venue/protocol fees are separate economic components; net outcome accounting should not collapse them into one network-fee field.
patterns: store observed total fee and version-specific fee components separately
keep tips and venue fees distinct
sources.overlap: Truth-X captures raw transaction `meta.fee`; execution economics exposes base/priority/tip components; paper simulator uses independent configured values. Finalized asset deltas now expose both transaction-wide network fee and fee charged to the observed wallet for legacy/v0, but the separate Version 1 wire decoder and end-to-end reconciliation across failed trades, tips and venue fees remain incomplete.
risks: estimated fee and realized network fee can diverge
unsuccessful transactions still incur network fees
fee schema may not represent future transaction versions

regress different transaction fee payer vs observed wallet and preserve gross delta
reconcile separate Jito tip transfers and venue fees to account deltas

The project has an explicit Start SYLPH check and read-only live status audit, but existing listeners predate some source-level ownership fixes, so checkout state and running-process state must be reported separately.
